program: [ [ mul ] swap cons ] map dup nil [ map 1 cons ] fold [ 0 eq? ] filter swap [ drop uncons drop ] fold [ 1 swap i ] map 0 [ add ] fold
notes: Named lists instead of a reset-on-zero fold: the multiplier closures, their suffix products (prefix-sum idiom with `map 1 cons`), the zero products (one per position before the last zero), the multipliers with that many dropped, their values (each applied to 1), the sum. The dropped prefix ends just before the last zero, which adds nothing.

program: [ 1 sub swap ] dip 1 add [ lt? ] swap cons filter swap [ swap lt? ] swap cons filter
notes: The inclusive bounds become strict (lo-1, hi+1), then one consed-bound filter per bound: entries below hi+1, then those above lo-1. Same algorithm as #155's staged witness; the lo-1 is folded into the first dip so each filter cycle fits in 8 ops.

program: [ quote [ add ] cat ] map [ quote ] map [ [ uncons ] swap cat ] map over [ quote ] map over [ drop nil ] map cat [ i map cat ] fold [ drop uncons drop ] fold
notes: Each y becomes the closure (uncons (y add)); xs become singletons padded with one nil per y, so a y past the end of xs maps over nil and appends nothing. The fold body `i map cat` pairs heads in order and appends the sums flat, and a fold over xs drops the |xs| leftover heads. Truncation needs no markers or filter.

program: nil quote swap [ 1 add ] map [ quote [ lt? ] cat ] map [ quote [ over ] cat ] map [ [ uncons swap ] cat ] map [ [ drop 1 ] cat ] map [ [ cons ] cat ] map swap [ i swap filter cons ] fold [ 0 [ add ] fold ] map nil [ cons ] fold uncons drop
notes: A history scan over list states with no flags: each x becomes Q = (x+1 lt?), then the closure (Q over uncons swap drop 1 cons), which pushes the previous state with a fresh 1 prepended. The fold body `i swap filter cons` filters it by Q (every 1 is kept iff x > 0, so a non-positive clears the run) and pushes it on the history. Then counts, reversed, seed dropped.

program: [ dup 1 sub ] dip [ lt? ] nil [ swap ] ifte [ drop ] dip over sub [ 1 sub ] dip [ [ sub ] swap cons ] dip 1 add 1 add [ map ] dip [ over sub mul ] swap cons map nil quote swap [ 1 add ] map [ quote [ lt? ] cat ] map [ quote [ over ] cat ] map [ [ uncons swap ] cat ] map [ [ drop 1 ] cat ] map [ [ cons ] cat ] map swap [ i swap filter cons ] fold [ 0 [ add ] fold ] map dup [ 1 sub quote ] map [ [ swap lt? ] cat ] map swap [ filter ] fold uncons swap drop
notes: hi is clamped to at least lo-1 (ordered-pair ifte), so lo > hi gives an empty interval and #155's lo <= hi precondition is gone. u = x-lo+1 and P = u(hi-lo+2-u), which is positive exactly inside. Then the same list-state history scan as running_positive_streaks with Q = (P+1 lt?), the run counts, and the filter-fold maximum. 135 ops against the fused 110; the cost is the per-position scan plus the maximum.
